title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for queueing fairness, starvation prevention, and adaptive timeouts
author: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: This PR tunes the continuous-batcher scheduler to reduce request starvation, improve fairness across priority classes, and introduce adaptive timeouts to prevent long-queued requests from delaying low-latency paths.
Motivation: production traces and canary runs showed occasional client-visible p95 spikes originating from the continuous batching queue when load is bursty and there is mixed priority traffic. Additionally, certain long KV-cache warmup requests could be starved by throughput-focused batching heuristics.
Goals: (1) introduce an aging mechanism so older requests gain scheduling weight, (2) bound per-priority queue length and ensure round-robin draining across priorities, (3) adaptive per-request timeouts that avoid excessive waiting while preserving batching efficiency, (4) minor kernel selection heuristic to prefer lower-latency ops under tight SLOs, (5) conservative rollout plan with feature flag and metrics/alerts.
Changes:
- scheduler/continuous_batcher.py: implement queue aging ( configurable aging_rate_ms ), per-priority buckets, and a batch selection algorithm that enforces max_wait_ms and max_queue_size per-priority.
- runtime/kv_cache.go: add hooks to expose KV-warmup progress and a fast-path flag so the scheduler can treat warmup requests as higher-importance for a short window.
- runtime/kernel_selector.rs: add a low-latency preference hint used by the scheduler to prefer fast kernels for batches with tight remaining SLO.
- tests/loadtest/continuous_batcher_starvation.py: synthetic microbench harness to reproduce starvation and verify fairness metrics.
- docs/perf/continuous-batcher-tuning.md: rationale, configuration knobs, recommended values, and rollout checklist.
- metrics: emit new metrics batcher.queue_age_ms, batcher.per_priority_queue_size, batcher.adaptive_timeout_ms, and an alerting rule proposal.
Config knobs added (defaults are conservative):
- continuous_batcher.aging_rate_ms = "20"
- continuous_batcher.max_queue_size_per_priority = "1024"
- continuous_batcher.max_wait_ms = "120"
- continuous_batcher.min_batch_size_for_latency_sensitive = "1"
- continuous_batcher.adaptive_timeout_base_ms = "30"
Benchmarks: Canary cluster tests and local perf runs against release candidate models show:
- p95 latency reduction for mixed-priority workloads: 12% on average
- throughput at 95th percentile load: +6-10% due to smarter batching (less head-of-line blocking)
- starvation incidents reproduced by loadtest harness reduced from 4/10 runs to 0/10 runs
- KV-cache warmup tail latency improved by ~18%
Safety & rollback: change guarded by runtime feature flag continuous_batcher.scheduler_v2 (off by default). CI includes unit tests, integration loadtest step, and linting. Rollout plan: enable on canary-gpu1 for 48h, monitor new metrics and alerts, then gradual rollout by region.
Related: builds on prior PRs for continuous-batcher timeout tuning (see PRs 41213, 45021) and is driven by Linear ENG-1984.
Checklist:

- [x] integration loadtest reproducer
- [x] metrics and docs
- [x] feature-flagged rollout
- [x] review and perf validation

review_comments: Arjun Patel: The aging algorithm looks reasonable but can you explain how you avoid oscillation between priorities when load is periodically bursty?
Maya Chen: We clamp aging_weight to a max value and apply a small hysteresis window (10ms) before changing target draining order; added explanation to docs and unit test to simulate burst patterns.
Sofia Martinez: CI showed a flaky integration test on the first run (timeout). Was that related to the max_wait_ms?
Maya Chen: That was due to an overly-tight default on canary; increased adaptive_timeout_base_ms from 10ms to 30ms and retriggered CI (see updated defaults).
Priya Rao: Please add observability for per-priority queue size and queue age percentiles so SREs can tune knobs live.
Maya Chen: Added batcher.per_priority_queue_size and batcher.queue_age_ms metrics and updated alert doc.
ci_log_summary: Initial CI: failed integration timeout (flaky test).
Update defaults + re-run: all checks passed (unit, lint, integration loadtest).
Post-merge: canary pipeline executed; no regressions observed.
release_notes: Scheduler: improved continuous-batcher fairness and starvation prevention with adaptive timeouts; new metrics for queue age and per-priority size; feature-flagged rollout.
notes: This PR is conservative in defaults to avoid regressions to latency-sensitive customers. The main knobs to tune in production are continuous_batcher.adaptive_timeout_base_ms and continuous_batcher.aging_rate_ms.
If an SLO-sensitive route sees regression, disable continuous_batcher.scheduler_v2 for that route and open SUP ticket referencing SUP-4721.
